experiments.title: Vote-from-your-newsletter: copyable email and Substack blocks with one link per option

items.title: Vote-from-your-newsletter: copyable email and Substack blocks with one link per option
items.why: Authors already ask their own lists to pick a cover by a deadline (Neve's Substack, Sara Foster, Alexis Grant's 4,000-subscriber list, where most of her votes came from the newsletter), and sellers and creators have Instagram audiences or email lists. A block of option images, each linking to its own vote, turns every click from a reader into a tiebreak visit and every poll creator into a distribu
acceptance: The poll page shows a 'Get votes from your newsletter' panel to the poll's creator only (same voter cookie or x-tiebreak-voter header). For a 3-option poll it offers two copy buttons: an HTML block (a <table> with inline styles, no <script>, no <style>, one <a href> per option wrapping that option's image or text, absolute URLs) and a Markdown/plain block (one image line plus one link line per option) for Substack and similar editors

Each option link has the form /polls/<id>?pick=<A|B|C|D>&src=newsletter. A GET of that URL records no vote: the vote count is unchanged after the GET, which keeps email link scanners and prefetchers from voting. The page opens with that option preselected and one 'Confirm vote' button, and confirming creates exactly one vote (Playwright, desktop and 390px phone)
A second confirm by the same voter returns 409 and the count doesn't change. A ?pick= link to a closed poll shows the result page, not a vote button
Landing on a ?src=newsletter link fires the visit beacon with the poll path and source 'newsletter', so these visits count apart from search and shared-link visits
No file under mobile/ changes in the PR, and the web and mobile CI checks pass

items.title: Opt-in public result pages for closed polls, indexed in the sitemap
items.why: PickFu publishes closed cover polls as indexable result pages, and they rank for queries like 'which book cover' (pickfu.com/books/book-covers/…), so buyers do search the questions themselves. tiebreak can do the same with real polls only: a creator ticks 'publish the result', and the closed poll becomes a page titled with its question. This is programmatic pages from user polls, which makes it a
acceptance: The create-poll form has a 'Publish the result when it closes' checkbox, off by default, and a private (paid) poll can't turn it on (the API returns 400 if both are set)

When an opted-in poll closes, /results/<slug> returns 200 with <title> and <h1> equal to the poll question, a meta description stating the winner and the vote count, every option with its vote split, and a 'Make your own tiebreak' link to the new-poll form
/results/<slug> for an open poll, an un-opted poll, or a poll hidden by 3 reports returns 404, and /sitemap.xml lists only opted-in, closed, unhidden polls
Loading /results/<slug> fires the visit beacon with path /results/<slug>
No file under mobile/ changes in the PR, and the web and mobile CI checks pass
